title: Marcos: No Pax Silica signing during Trump's ASEAN visit
summary: The Philippines will not sign the Pax Silica agreement during US President Donald Trump's visit for the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations Summit, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. said on…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines will not sign the Pax Silica agreement during US President Donald Trump's visit for the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations Summit, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. said on Wednesday, November 18.
The agreement would formalize the country's participation in the US-led initiative to secure global semiconductor and artificial intelligence supply chains.

Lee Lipton, US ambassador to the Philippines, earlier said that there would be no announcement on the project during the ASEAN Summit this month, but the country's Board of Investments expects the signing to take place before the end of 2026.

Under the agreement, a 4,000-acre industrial center would be built in the Luzon Economic Corridor, beginning with a 1,620-hectare site in New Clark City, Tarlac, which has drawn criticism over alleged environmental degradation and the displacement of farming and fishing communities. The Philippines hub would be the first site developed among members of the Pax Silica consortium.

The Institute for Climate and Sustainable Cities has described messaging surrounding the initiative as "mixed," saying that important details, such as control over the hub and its products and its environmental impact, remain unclear even as negotiations progress.
Pax Silica is also being oversimplified into an “arms race” between the US and China, organization Executive Director Angelo Kairos dela Cruz said.

Several progressive groups, including renowned Swedish climate activist Greta Thunberg, have called for the rejection of the project. Protests against Pax Silica have also been held during the summit.

Over 200 individuals were arrested at a protest against the initiative and Trump's visit in Sucat, Muntinlupa, on Sunday, November 15. The 276 protesters, including at least 50 students from the University of the Philippines system, were in police custody for more than two days at Camp Bagong Diwa in Taguig City after a delay in inquest proceedings.
In a report of GMA News, the National Capital Region Police Office said the detainees' transfer to the detention facility was being processed.
